$comment: Geometry recipes (pipeline/transit_pipeline/past.py): the Central Pacific's lines off today's track.

cp-port-costa-benicia-ferry.note: Port Costa's slip read off the 1898 Karquines sheet; Benicia's at the end of the waterfront track

cp-benicia-waterfront.note: Cut where it meets today's track near Army Point. OpenHistoricalMap's way was traced from the 1902 Napa sheet (1:125,000); on the 1952 sheet it lies along the waterfront track

cp-niles-livermore.note: OpenHistoricalMap's ways, traced from the 1906 Pleasanton sheet; checked on the 1953 sheets, from photographs of 1948-49, while the track was still there

cp-livermore-altamont.note: OpenHistoricalMap's way, traced from the 1907 Tesla sheet; checked on the 1953 sheets

cp-niles-san-jose.note: OpenHistoricalMap's ways, traced from the 1906 Pleasanton and 1897 San Jose sheets

sp-martinez-county-line.note: Today's Union Pacific Tracy Subdivision, the line of 1878, from Martinez by Avon, Port Chicago, Pittsburg, Antioch, Brentwood and Byron to the San Joaquin County line at Old River (decision 16); realignments since 1878 are checked only on the sheets of 1908-51. Today's Gold Runner uses the track as far as Bay Point
